draft.why_angle: The cited BLUETTI pages and the size tables shoppers see pair panel watts with battery kWh, but none says how many sunny days a bundle's panels need to refill its battery after the inverter's own idle draw. This page works that out for each bundle: 4.9 days for a 400 W bundle against 2.2 days for the kit, and it checks that the panels fit the Apex 300's 60 V solar inputs.

page.title: Tiny Home Solar Power Kit: Panels That Refill the Battery in 2.2 Days
page.h1: Tiny home solar power kit: size the panels to refill the battery
page.desc: An off-grid tiny home solar kit (BLUETTI Apex 300, B500K battery, two 500 W panels) whose panels refill 7,884.8 Wh in about 2.2 sunny days after inverter idle loss.
page.answer: Short answer. The off-grid tiny home solar power kit to buy: BLUETTI Apex 300 inverter, B500K battery and two 500 W panels. After the inverter's 20 W idle draw, 4 sun-hours leave 3,520 Wh a day, refilling the 7,884.8 Wh battery from empty in about 2.2 days.

page.after:
What the differences mean

The inverter's idle loss comes off the top every day, before the battery gets anything: 20 W × 24 h = 480 Wh. That is 6.1% of the kit's 7,884.8 Wh (480 ÷ 7,884.8).

Kit refill: 1,000 W × 4 h = 4,000 Wh, minus 480 Wh, leaves 3,520 Wh a day, and 7,884.8 ÷ 3,520 = 2.2 days from empty.

The 400 W bundle: 400 W × 4 h = 1,600 Wh, minus 480 Wh, leaves 1,120 Wh, and 5,529.6 ÷ 1,120 = 4.9 days. Its panels have to cover the same 480 Wh idle loss out of less than half the output.

With a duller sun: Impulse Gamer averaged closer to 400 W per SORA 500 in Australian winter. 2 × 400 W × 4 h = 3,200 Wh, minus 480 Wh, leaves 2,720 Wh, and 7,884.8 ÷ 2,720 = 2.9 days.

Price per stored Wh: the kit is $4,796 for 7,884.8 Wh. The 2×B300K bundle is $5,499 for 8,294.4 Wh, so the extra 409.6 Wh costs $703.

Full-time, hardwired by an installer, 240 V well pump or mini-splitSun Gold Power SGR-8K10E: 10,240 Wh, 3,600 W of panels {buy:sungoldpower-sgr-8k10e-off-grid-solar-kit}

Why panel watts decide whether the battery keeps up

A battery sized for several days of power only helps if the panels can refill it between cloudy spells. BLUETTI says the Apex 300 cuts idle loss to 20 W. That loss runs around the clock, so a small array spends most of its output keeping the inverter on.

Panel count is limited by the inputs. Notebookcheck lists the Apex 300's built-in solar inputs as 2× XT60 at 12–60 V and 20 A each. Impulse Gamer lists the SORA 500 at 49.1 V open-circuit and 13.31 A short-circuit, so one panel goes on each input. That makes 1,000 W the most the built-in inputs take from these panels. BLUETTI's 4,000 W solar figure carries the footnote 'Requires a SolarX 4K'.

Buying the items separately is cheaper than the store's bundles. The Apex 300 on its own ($1,499), the B500K for Apex 300/200 ($1,599) and two SORA 500 panels ($849 each) come to $4,796. The store's 'Apex 300 + B500K' option is $3,299, against $3,098 for the two items, and its 2×B300K + 2×500W bundle is $5,499.

The kit: Apex 300 + B500K + 2× SORA 500 {kit:kit-tiny-home-solar}

If you're hardwiring with an installer, the Sun Gold Power SGR-8K10E gives more of everything for $4,949: 3,600 W of panels, which the maker rates at 14.4 kWh a day at 4 full-sun hours, a 10,240 Wh battery and an 8,000 W 120/240 V inverter. The listing doesn't give its inverter's idle draw, so its refill time above is before that loss.

Not recommended

Apex 300 + B300K + 2×200W ($3,499). Its 400 W of panels leave 1,120 Wh a day after the 20 W idle loss, so the 5,529.6 Wh battery takes 4.9 sunny days to refill from empty. On the same store, the Apex 300 + B300K ($2,599) plus the 2×200W panel pack ($798) is $3,397, which is $102 less for the same set.
